reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that coherent nanoprecipitates in W-based HEAs can improve strength and ductility, but it provides no data or discussion on thermal conductivity, electron-mediated heat transfer, or the specific B2 phase and 900°C heat treatment proposed. The key premises regarding heat transfer enhancement and the specific thermal conductivity improvement are entirely unsupported.
premises: Coherent B2 nanoprecipitates can be formed in W-based refractory HEAs by a post-sintering heat treatment at ~900°C
These nanoprecipitates enhance electron-mediated heat transfer (thermal conductivity)
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces minimize electron scattering
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion and maintain/improve mechanical strength under cyclic high-temperature loading
The treatment yields ~20% improvement in thermal conductivity while retaining/enhancing yield strength and ductility at 800–1000°C
